observation.title: Asset Watch
observation.chartDescription: Daily prices and drawdowns from their running peak, with zoom controls
observation.chartNote: Drawdown uses the running historical peak on the selected basis. Changing the chart period does not reset the peak.
observation.closeOnly: This source provides closing prices, which are used for both highs and lows.
observation.methodologyText: The peak refers only to available history, which may not cover the full life of the asset. Drawdown = latest daily price / peak − 1; recovery gain = peak / latest daily price − 1. Maximum drawdown uses closing prices over all available history. An unfinished daily bar can change.
observation.reboundMethod: The drawdown low is the lowest price among daily bars after the peak day, including the latest bar. The selected basis uses intraday lows or closing prices. Rebound = latest daily price ÷ drawdown low price − 1.
observation.returnMethod: Returns use calendar-day lookbacks and the last session on or before the reference date. Insufficient history is shown as —. Data does not poll automatically; refresh to request the latest available data. Free feeds may be delayed.
observation.indexMethod: Indices use native index points, without substituting ETFs or CFDs. Back-calculated pre-launch history may be included; coverage does not imply the launch date.
observation.hstechSources: Hang Seng TECH uses Eastmoney daily data first, with Sina and other existing sources as fallbacks. Bitget also offers an HSTECH CFD market API. Its bid/ask prices differ from index points and are not mixed into these peak calculations.

chartWorkspace.guideMaIntro: MA averages prices over a chosen number of bars to show their overall direction and reduce the effect of individual candles.
chartWorkspace.guideMaUse: A rising average with price above it indicates relative strength; the reverse indicates relative weakness. Crossovers can help identify direction changes but often repeat in sideways markets.
chartWorkspace.guideMaParameters: Length counts bars on the current chart: 20 means the latest 20 bars. Shorter lengths react faster; longer lengths are smoother. Source chooses the price used in the calculation. Offset changes the display position only.
chartWorkspace.guideEmaIntro: EMA gives recent prices more weight, so it responds faster than an MA of the same length.
chartWorkspace.guideEmaUse: Read its slope, price relative to the line, and crossings between faster and slower averages. Short-term fluctuations also move the EMA, and a crossover does not guarantee a continuing trend.
chartWorkspace.guideEmaParameters: Length counts bars on the current chart. Short lengths react faster; long lengths are smoother. Source chooses the input price, offset shifts the plot, and color distinguishes multiple averages.
chartWorkspace.guideRsiIntro: RSI compares the size of recent gains and losses to express price momentum on a 0–100 scale. It is neither a percentage return nor a probability of rising prices.
chartWorkspace.guideRsiUse: 70 and 30 are common reference levels for strong and weak momentum; 50 helps compare relative strength. Crossing 70 does not mean price must fall, and crossing 30 does not mean it must rise. Strong trends can keep RSI near an extreme.
chartWorkspace.guideRsiParameters: Shorter lengths respond faster and longer lengths are smoother. Length counts bars, so changing the chart timeframe also changes the amount of real time covered.
chartWorkspace.guideVolumeIntro: VOL shows the quantity traded during each bar. Its unit depends on the feed; spot crypto feeds commonly report units of the base currency.
chartWorkspace.guideVolumeUse: Compare recent volume alongside price: higher volume means more activity and lower volume means less. Bar colors follow the candle direction; they do not separate exact buying and selling volumes.
chartWorkspace.guideVolumeParameters: Adjust the colors of rising and falling bars. Volume is raw data for each interval rather than a moving average; changing the timeframe changes the period represented by each column.
chartWorkspace.guideBollIntro: BOLL combines a central moving average with upper and lower bands based on standard deviation, showing relative price position and volatility.
chartWorkspace.guideBollUse: Narrowing bands indicate less recent volatility; widening bands indicate more. Touching a band does not require a reversal: strong trends can continue along a band.
chartWorkspace.guideBollParameters: Length sets the statistical window, and the standard deviation multiplier sets the distance from the middle line. Higher multipliers widen the bands. Source chooses the input price.
chartWorkspace.guideMacdIntro: MACD uses the difference between a fast and a slow EMA, plus a signal line, to show changes in trend and momentum. Its histogram shows the gap between the two lines.
chartWorkspace.guideMacdUse: Observe line crossovers, their position relative to zero, and whether the histogram expands or contracts. A shrinking histogram means the gap is narrowing, not that price has already reversed.
chartWorkspace.guideMacdParameters: Fast and slow lengths set the two EMAs. Signal length smooths their difference. Shorter settings react faster and are also more sensitive to short-term fluctuations.
chartWorkspace.guideAtrIntro: ATR measures the size of recent price fluctuations. It describes volatility, not whether price is rising or falling.
chartWorkspace.guideAtrUse: Rising ATR means larger recent bar ranges; falling ATR means smaller ranges. ATR uses price units, so raw values are not directly comparable across instruments with different price levels.
chartWorkspace.guideAtrParameters: Length controls the smoothing window. Shorter lengths respond faster; longer lengths are steadier. Changing the chart timeframe changes what each ATR observation represents.
chartWorkspace.guideVwapIntro: VWAP is a volume-weighted average price: prices traded with more volume have greater weight. It represents the average traded price over the chosen period.
chartWorkspace.guideVwapUse: Price above VWAP is above that period's weighted average; price below it is below the average. It provides a relative reference without guaranteeing a bounce or reversal.
chartWorkspace.guideVwapParameters: Anchor determines when accumulation begins or resets, and source chooses the input price. Use the same anchor and period when comparing VWAP values.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxIntro: This chart shows ADX, +DI and −DI together, a combination also called DMI. ADX measures trend strength; the other lines help identify direction.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxAdx: Blue ADX: rising values mean a stronger trend, not necessarily rising prices. A downtrend can also have high ADX.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxPlusDi: Green +DI: upward directional strength. Above −DI, it indicates relatively stronger upward movement.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxMinusDi: Red −DI: downward directional strength. Above +DI, it indicates relatively stronger downward movement.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxUse: Compare +DI and −DI for direction, then use ADX for strength. Optional levels such as 30 and 10 mark your chosen strength ranges; crossings are not automatic trade signals. Smoothing causes the indicator to lag price.
chartWorkspace.guideAdxParameters: DI length sets the direction window; ADX smoothing controls the blue line. Shorter periods respond faster. Both reference lines start off; enable either in Reference lines and choose its value. Enabled levels are horizontal dashed lines.

researchUi.accountBasis: Continuous closing account equity in UTC, including unrealized P&L and actual position size. Missing boundary marks carry forward the last earlier equity, with its time shown. Capital does not restart annually and returns are not grouped by exit year.
researchUi.accountBasisUnavailable: This older result has no equity series at the selected frequency. Signal-bar equity cannot substitute for execution-bar drawdown.
researchUi.normalizedBasis: Each actual trade is normalized to equal entry principal, without compounding or changing the position path. This is not a new simulation of account returns.
researchUi.drawdownBasis: Peaks, troughs and recovery use saved closing equity only. Intrabar price order is not inferred.
researchUi.realizedBasis: Realized P&L is grouped by exit date in the account currency. It is not an annually reset or mark-to-market return. Holding time uses entry and exit times; intrabar timing is unknown. Exit reasons identify settlement triggers, not necessarily causes of loss.
researchUi.tradeComparisonBasis: Trades match by exact entry time, direction and order at that time. Different entry times count as added or removed trades. Price and return comparisons ignore floating-point differences of 1e-12. P&L uses equal principal; changes in account capital alone do not imply different trading rules.
researchUi.timelineBasis: Events retain their original times and phases. Intrabar times identify the containing bar, not individual tick times. Protection update and effective times follow saved events.
researchUi.runUnavailableHint: The research summary is preserved, but the original backtest run is missing. Restore it and check again to view trades and equity details.

backendText.adaptive_cloud_description: Original follows the supplied Pine rules; cross is a crossover candidate inferred from screenshots. Preserve indicators and conditions for each bar; TP/SL labels are not trade orders.
backendText.adaptive_cloud_warmup_rule_explanation: Use the largest history requirement under the current parameters. Reduce EMA/RMA initialization weight below 1e-8 and cover declared lookbacks. This numerical initialization standard does not guarantee identical prices or signals.
backendText.adaptive_cloud_parameter_constraints_0_m: The original Pine rules require the closing price for the average
backendText.cross_market_trend_v1_name: Cross-asset trend benchmark v1: breakout, dual averages and direction
backendText.cross_market_trend_v1_description: Enter and exit on the selected timeframe, with a fixed ATR14 initial stop and no additional percentage profit protection.
backendText.ma_cross_description: Enter long on an upward crossover and short on a downward crossover. Close the existing position before reversing.
backendText.ma_cross_parameter_constraints_0_message: Fast average period must be shorter than slow average period
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_name: Channel: ATR stop and reversal confirmation v5 (research)
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_description: Keep v4 separate. Set an ATR initial stop and wait for consecutive closing confirmations before a reversal exit.
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_parameters_ch: Maximum entry distance from center / W (0: unlimited)
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_parameters_in: Initial range stop / W (0 disables; alternative to fixed stop)
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_parameters_at: Initial stop ATR multiplier (0: original stop)
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_parameters_re: Consecutive closes required for reversal exit
backendText.trend_cloud_atr_confirm_v5_rules_0: Compare center period, width, breakout threshold, chase distance, profit protection and initial stop. Defaults reproduce the previous highest-return configuration.
backendText.trend_cloud_comparison_description: Compare original reversals, screenshot crossover candidates, high-low channels and average benchmarks. Reverse positions without pyramiding; TP/SL labels are not orders.
backendText.trend_cloud_comparison_parameters_long_o: Long only (short signals close the position)
backendText.trend_cloud_context_v3_name: Trend channel: support, momentum and trend v3
backendText.trend_cloud_context_v3_description: Preserve channel entries and exits. Add confirmed 1-hour support/resistance, 1-hour RSI momentum and 4-hour trend filters individually or together.
backendText.trend_cloud_context_v3_parameters_record: Save levels and conditions visible at the time
backendText.trend_cloud_context_v3_rules_1: Includes confirmed higher-timeframe support/resistance. Preserve at least 650 context bars and increase warmup for longer averages.
backendText.trend_cloud_direct_v7_name: Original channel: direct adaptation research v7
backendText.trend_cloud_direct_v7_parameters_adaptiv: Adapt average speed to directional price efficiency
backendText.trend_cloud_direct_v7_parameters_scaled_: Initial stop at 2 ATR; activate protection at 4 ATR
backendText.trend_cloud_direct_v7_parameters_atr_tra: After activation, exit on a 2 ATR pullback from peak
backendText.trend_cloud_direct_v7_parameters_efficie: Require 31-bar directional efficiency of at least 0.2
backendText.trend_cloud_entry_v2_description: Fix EMA31, a 0.8 width threshold and a 20% eight-hour efficiency filter. Keep exits at 50% giveback after 2% profit or a reversal signal; compare only entry conditions.
backendText.trend_cloud_experiments_name: Trend channel: ATR and loss diagnostics
backendText.trend_cloud_experiments_description: Change one condition at a time. Evaluate at close and fill at the next open; entry filters do not block reversal exits. These experiments do not establish the screenshot source code.
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_confirmation_v1_nam: EMA55 accumulated signal intrabar breakout v1
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_confirmation_v1_des: Record the level at the original signal close. Enter on an intrabar breakout from the next bar; reverse signals reset the pending signal, which can be used once.
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_confirmation_v1_par: 0 means unlimited; 2 waits only for the two bars after the original signal.
Event order in the entry bar
Treat the adverse extreme as preceding entry
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_confirmation_v2_nam: EMA channel accumulated signal intrabar breakout v2
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_exit_v4_name: EMA channel intrabar confirmation: reversal exit toggle v4
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_exit_v4_parameters_: Trade only with the center-line direction over the last 6 bars
Exit on reverse signal; disabling prevents reversals while holding
After a stop, allow one re-entry beyond the stopped bar extremes
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_support_v1_name: EMA channel intrabar confirmation with support/resistance v1
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_support_v1_descript: Add known support/resistance checks to the original 15-minute signals. Filter new entries only; preserve reversal exits and two-bar intrabar confirmation.
backendText.trend_cloud_intrabar_support_v1_paramete: Require the original signal near support or resistance
backendText.trend_cloud_manual_v1_name: Trend channel: manual-trading win-rate study v1
backendText.trend_cloud_manual_v1_description: Use EMA31 for center and width, break out at 0.8 widths and stop chasing beyond 2 widths. Compare confirmation, retest entries and profit protection; reversal signals can always close positions.
backendText.trend_cloud_manual_v1_parameters_retest_: Maximum bars to wait for a retest after breakout
backendText.trend_cloud_manual_v1_parameters_efficie: Minimum net movement / total movement over eight hours
backendText.trend_cloud_profit_protection_name: Trend channel: profit protection or reversal exit
backendText.trend_cloud_profit_protection_descriptio: Use EMA31 for center with adjustable width and trigger multipliers. Do not chase distant breakouts. Reverse signals close positions; after activation, the specified profit giveback also closes them. The exit conditions work independently.
backendText.trend_cloud_reverse_after_protection_v5_: EMA channel: profit-gated reversal exit v5
Use the original intrabar confirmation rules. Optionally require active profit protection before accepting a new reversal exit; do not reverse before the threshold is reached.
Allow reversal exits only after profit protection activates
backendText.trend_cloud_robustness_v1_description: Preserve profit-protection and reversal exits. Test slow-trend filters, efficiency filters, entry spacing and blocking repeated same-direction entries separately. Keep the previous strategy available.
backendText.trend_cloud_robustness_v1_parameters_met: Slow average: integer period at least 2; efficiency: 0 to 1; spacing: positive integer bars.
backendText.trend_cloud_robustness_v1_parameter_cons: Filter parameter does not match the selected method; follow its guidance
backendText.trend_cloud_signal_confirmation_v1_name: EMA55 accumulated original signal confirmation v1
backendText.trend_cloud_signal_confirmation_v1_descr: Remember the original entry signal. Enter only after a later close breaks its close, wick or body; an opposite signal cancels the pending one.
backendText.trend_cloud_signal_confirmation_v1_param: Save original signals, waiting state and confirmation conditions
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_name: EMA channel: delayed stop and stop-bar zone restriction v1
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_descrip: Use the original body breakout entry. Confirm the initial stop at the next open, intrabar or close; optionally suspend new entries inside the stopped bar range.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_paramet: Evaluate at the next open after touch
Evaluate at the next open and intrabar after touch
Evaluate at the next close after touch
After a stop, pause re-entry inside the stopped bar range
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_rules_0: Next bar always means the signal timeframe; finer data only controls fills. Delayed stops can lose more than the nominal stop distance.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_rules_1: Reversal exits and profit protection are not delayed. Only initial-stop exits establish a restricted entry zone.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v1_rules_2: After a stop, freeze the high-low range at the signal-bar close. A later closing breakout can accumulate one new same-direction signal, retaining confirmation and chase limits.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v2_name: EMA channel: finer-timeframe stop confirmation v2
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v2_descrip: Use 15-minute entry signals. The initial stop may wait for confirmation on the execution timeframe; select the profit-protection frequency in the backtest configuration.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v2_rules_0: Use the explicitly selected signal or execution timeframe for next-bar stop confirmation. Missing finer data follows the recorded fallback policy; delayed stops can exceed the nominal loss.
backendText.trend_cloud_stop_confirmation_v2_rules_3: The restricted zone remains the stopped signal bar high-low range; 5-minute stop confirmation does not change it.
backendText.trend_cloud_width_reentry_v1_name: EMA55 width and post-stop re-entry v1
backendText.trend_cloud_width_reentry_v1_description: Compare predefined rules: original, outer-line entry, width switching, width-based stops and one post-stop re-entry.
backendText.trend_cloud_width_reentry_v1_parameters_: Adjust the initial stop to relative channel width
Allow one same-direction re-entry after the initial stop
Width reference bars (about one day on 15-minute data)
Relative width to enter outer-line mode
Relative width to return to original mode

backendText.repairedHistory: Checked {symbol} history and filled available missing ranges
backendText.noMacroHistory: Not enough macro history yet. Refresh the data to calculate a dollar-liquidity score.
backendText.macroDescription_FED_BALANCE: A shrinking Fed balance sheet withdraws base liquidity.
backendText.macroDescription_TGA: A rising TGA drains reserves from the banking system.
backendText.macroDescription_ONRRP: A higher ON RRP balance means more cash remains in Fed facilities.
backendText.macroDescription_SOFR_IORB: SOFR rising relative to IORB indicates greater repo funding pressure.
backendText.macroDescription_SRF_USAGE: Greater SRF usage indicates demand for central-bank repo liquidity.
backendText.macroDescription_BANK_CASH_BUFFER: A falling cash-to-assets ratio reduces commercial banks’ intermediation buffer.
backendText.macroDescription_HY_SPREAD: Wider credit spreads indicate tighter private-sector financing conditions.
backendText.macroDescription_VIX: Higher US equity implied volatility indicates more risk aversion and deleveraging pressure.
backendText.macroDescription_DXY: A stronger dollar generally tightens global dollar liquidity.
backendText.macroDescription_US10Y_REAL: Higher real yields increase discount-rate pressure on risk-asset valuations.
backendText.macroDescription_NET_LIQUIDITY: Fed assets minus TGA and ON RRP; a supplementary observation excluded from the composite score.
backendText.macroDescription_M2: A broad-money observation excluded from the composite score.
backendText.previewLocalOnly: Checks local cache timestamps only. The earliest cached date is not the exchange listing date. Missing data is fetched at runtime; this preview does not download prices or submit a run.
backendText.previewCoverage: Comparable intervals have continuous local data and full warmup coverage. They do not replace the requested interval. Prices, lower-timeframe OHLC alignment and the final snapshot are validated at runtime.
